description:
A “to do”list is used in QuickBooks to keep track of tasks. Notice the Notes field: when you do a query on the ToDo list (ToDoQuery), you can use the supplied name filters to search these Notes and filter by them.

The `to_do_add` wrapper from qbXML is also accepted. Returns the v2 request to send, and the webhook payload QuickBooks' answer arrives in (this operation's response_json: its data shape and the status codes to handle).

Possible errors (error.code / error.type; the call result explains each): 1030 unsupported_request, 3000 invalid_object_id, 3040 invalid_amount, 3070 string_too_long, 3120 object_not_found, 3140 invalid_reference, 3150 missing_element, 3175 in_use, 3176 locked, 3180 cannot_save, 3210 invalid_value, 3220 not_authorized, 3231 request_not_processed, 3250 feature_not_enabled, 3260 insufficient_permission, 3261 personal_data_access_denied, 3262 payroll_subscription_required, 3263 read_only_access, 3264 merchant_services_subscription_required, 3270 missing_posting_account

customer_ref.description:
`customer_ref` identifies a customer or customer job. If both `full_name` and `list_id` are provided, `full_name` is ignored. In SalesReceipt and ReceivePayment, it identifies who receives credit.

Choose at most one of: `customer_ref`, or `employee_ref`, or `lead_ref`, or `vendor_ref`.

full_name.description: The record's name, parents first: `Jones:Kitchen:Cabinets`. Not case-sensitive.

list_id.description: QuickBooks' ID for the record. Used over `full_name` when both are sent.

employee_ref.description:
The employee list contains payroll information about each of the company’s employees.

Choose at most one of: `customer_ref`, or `employee_ref`, or `lead_ref`, or `vendor_ref`.

full_name.description: The record's name, parents first: `Jones:Kitchen:Cabinets`. Not case-sensitive.

list_id.description: QuickBooks' ID for the record. Used over `full_name` when both are sent.

include_qbxml.description: Also return the qbXML this compiles to, for debugging. Not part of the v2 request.

is_active.description: If `is_active` is true, this object is currently enabled for use by QuickBooks. The default value is true.

is_done.description: If `is_done` is true, this “to do” task has been completed. The default value of `is_done` is false.

lead_ref.description:
The lead list contains information about leads for a company.

Choose at most one of: `customer_ref`, or `employee_ref`, or `lead_ref`, or `vendor_ref`.

full_name.description: The record's name, parents first: `Jones:Kitchen:Cabinets`. Not case-sensitive.

list_id.description: QuickBooks' ID for the record. Used over `full_name` when both are sent.

priority.description: Priority may have one of the following values: Low [DEFAULT], Medium, High

reminder_date.description: The date on which the contents of the Notes string will appear on the Reminder list within QuickBooks.

reminder_time.description: The time on which the contents of the Notes string will appear on the Reminder list within QuickBooks.

request_id.description: Your own label for the request, sent to QuickBooks as its qbXML `requestID` and echoed in the raw answer (`response_xml`); optional, since the answer's webhook already carries the request's `id`.

type.description: Type may have one of the following values: Task [DEFAULT], Call, Fax, Email, Meeting, Appointment

vendor_ref.description:
A vendor is any person or company from whom a small business owner buys goods and services. (Banks and tax agencies usually are included on the vendor list.)

Choose at most one of: `customer_ref`, or `employee_ref`, or `lead_ref`, or `vendor_ref`.

full_name.description: The record's name, parents first: `Jones:Kitchen:Cabinets`. Not case-sensitive.

list_id.description: QuickBooks' ID for the record. Used over `full_name` when both are sent.
